content.title: Programme characteristics and components (heart failure care)
Characteristics: Flexible focus including prevention of disease progression, symptom control, and maintaining patients in preferred place of care for end-stage heart failure
Encourage patient/carer engagement in understanding and managing their condition
Components: Optimized management: lifestyle choices, pharmacological treatments, and devices
Patient education with emphasis on self-care and symptom management
Provision of psychosocial support to patients and family caregivers
Follow-up after discharge (clinic; home visits; telephone support or telemonitoring)
Easy access to healthcare, especially to prevent and manage decompensation

Assessment of (and appropriate intervention in response to) unexplained changes in weight, nutritional and functional status, quality of life, sleep problems, psychosocial problems or other findings (e.g., laboratory values)
Access to advanced treatment options; supportive and palliative care
content.Section_heading_next: 9.3 Patient education, self-care and lifestyle advice
content.Section_note: Adequate patient self-care is essential for effective management of HF and to enable patients to understand beneficial actions and agree to self-monitoring and management plans.
